<thought>Based on the observed isotopic pattern—a dominant M peak at m/z 276 with an M+2 peak at m/z 278 at roughly one‑third the intensity, a classic 3:1 ratio characteristic of a single chlorine atom—we can definitively identify chlorine. The relatively large M+1 peak (~16 % of the base) matches the expected contribution from multiple carbon atoms (≈15 C atoms give ~16 % M+1), allowing us to definitively identify carbon as well. No other element shows a distinctive pattern (e.g., bromine’s 1:1 M:M+2). Therefore the definitively identifiable elements are carbon and chlorine.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'Cl']</final_answer>
